title: Log SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl's schedule-JSON decode failure instead of silently swallowing it
why: If a stage's schedule JSON column is ever malformed (migration bug, manual DB edit, a bad sync-merge write), every read of that stage silently substitutes a hardcoded delay_days:0 default with zero AppLogger call — changing that stage's chazara/review timing with no diagnostic trail to explain a future 'my review schedule looks wrong' report. SchedulerStageRepositoryImpl also has no dedicated unit test file (grep across test/ confirms it is only exercised indirectly, with well-formed data, through SchedulerEngine/DailyTaskGenerator integration tests), so this fallback path is completely unexercised by the suite.
recommendation: Log via AppLogger (including the row id and raw schedule string) in the catch before falling back, and add a unit test for the fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: The catch in _rowToSchedulerStage calls AppLogger.warning/error with the stage row id and raw schedule string before falling back to the default.
New unit test constructs a StageDefinition row with malformed schedule JSON and asserts both the fallback SchedulerStage values and that the log call fired.
